item.title: How Qatar Became the Richest Country on Earth
item.description: Qatar went from pearl divers and poverty to GDP per capita above $80,000 on liquefied natural gas. The story of the North Field, the 2022 World Cup, and the tiny state that bought global influence.

item.title: How Did Dubai Get So Rich? (It's Not the Oil)
item.description: Dubai's oil is nearly gone — under 1% of GDP. So how did Dubai get so rich? Ports, planes, free zones, and a ruling family that bet everything on trade.

item.title: How Did South Korea Get So Rich? The $67 Miracle
item.description: In 1953, South Korea's GDP per capita was $67 — poorer than Ghana. How did South Korea get so rich? A dictator, discipline, and an industrial bet like no other.

item.title: Richest Country in Europe: The Full Ranking Explained
item.description: Which is the richest country in Europe? It depends how you count. The per-capita ranking — Luxembourg, Ireland, Switzerland — and why tiny countries always win.

item.title: Why Is Ireland So Rich? The Leprechaun Economics Truth
item.description: Ireland's GDP per capita tops $100,000 — but economists call it "leprechaun economics." Why is Ireland so rich on paper, and how much of it is real? Explained.

item.title: Why Is Luxembourg So Rich? Europe's $140,000 Secret
item.description: Luxembourg's GDP per capita tops $140,000 — higher than the US. The secret isn't luck: it's steel, then banking, then a plan to run the world's fund industry.

item.title: Why Is Norway So Rich? The $2 Trillion Oil Fund
item.description: Norway found oil in 1969 and did the opposite of every other oil nation — it saved the money. The result: a $2 trillion fund and GDP per capita above $90,000.

item.title: What Are Tax Havens and How Do They Hide Trillions?
item.description: An estimated $3.55 trillion in untaxed wealth hides offshore. From a five-story Cayman building housing 40,000 companies to the Panama Papers — how the offshore machine really works.

item.title: How Singapore Became Richer Than America
item.description: In 1965 Singapore was expelled from Malaysia with $500 per person. Today it produces $94,897 per person — more than the United States. Here is the blueprint.

item.title: Why Is Switzerland So Rich? The $107,702 Secret
item.description: Switzerland produces $107,702 per person — more than America — with no oil, no coastline, and 60% mountains. Here is the real story of the Swiss money machine.
